claims.text: Machine learning-based process optimization can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in conventionally processed materials.
Machine learning can predict and guide processing conditions that increase strength while maintaining ductility.
The optimized process will increase strength from 500 MPa to 600 MPa, a 20% increase.
The optimized process will retain at least 80% of baseline ductility, changing ductility from 20% to 16%.
The relevant temperature range for machine-learning optimization is 500-700°C.
The relevant pressure range for machine-learning optimization is 100-300 MPa.
The relevant processing-time range for machine-learning optimization is 1-5 hours.
Machine-learning-guided processing can refine the grain size to 1-5 μm.
Machine-learning-guided processing can produce a preferred crystal texture.
Optimized processing conditions control grain refinement and texture.
Controlled grain refinement and texture optimization lead to improved strength while maintaining ductility.
The conventional-processing baseline has a strength of 500 MPa.
The conventional-processing baseline has a ductility of 20%.
Machine-learning accuracy and training-data quality may affect the predicted outcome.
Microstructural complexity and variation in processing conditions may introduce outcome variability.

contradictions.description: The stated prediction is a 20% strength increase to 600 MPa, but the experiment only falsifies increases below 15% or 575 MPa; results from 575 MPa to below 600 MPa would miss the stated prediction without falsifying it.

The stated prediction requires retaining at least 80% of baseline ductility, or 16%, but falsification occurs only below 70%, or 14%; ductility from 14% to below 16% would miss the prediction without falsifying it.
